– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test method testBase64EmptyInputStream tests the behavior of base64 encoding an empty byte array. The input is emptyEncoded = new byte[0] and the expected output is also an empty byte array (emptyDecoded = new byte[0]). However, the current bug report states that encoding an empty byte array does not return an empty array but instead returns CRLF (line terminator characters).

Looking into the encode(byte[]) method's implementation, it delegates to the encodeBase64 method with chunking and URL safe options. The encodeBase64 method has an explicit check at lines 683-685 to return the input binaryData unchanged if it is null or length 0. This means if the input array is empty, it should directly return the empty array, satisfying the test.

However, the test is failing, which implies this check might not be consistently respected or the later encode method is adding the CRLF.

In the encode(byte[], int, int) method, the encoder processes input bytes and on EOF (inAvail < 0), it finalizes encoding by padding based on the remaining bytes and appending a line separator (CRLF) if chunking is enabled (line 446-449). But since the input length is 0, the encoder never processes any bytes in the else block (starting at line 450). On EOF, however, it still appends the lineSeparator if lineLength > 0.

This suggests that when the input array is empty, encodeBase64 returns an empty array early (line 684), but when called via the instance's encode() method with chunking enabled, the encoder still appends a CRLF line separator upon EOF, even though there was no actual data to encode, leading to the observed CRLF output.

Therefore, the root cause is that the encoder appends a CRLF line separator at EOF even for no input bytes, instead of returning an empty array as expected for empty input.

No relevant information in the recent bug reports.

This explains why the test expects an empty array but gets CRLF instead.

The method needing a fix is the encode(byte[], int, int) method or the logic controlling line separator insertion on EOF for empty input.

The initial null/empty check in encodeBase64 is correct but downstream logic contradicts it when chunking is enabled.

Hence, the defect lies in the encoding finalization code that is appending CRLF at EOF even with zero input data.

Suggested fix: prevent the encoder from appending CRLF if no bytes were encoded at all (modulus is zero and no chunks have been output). This logic belongs in the encode(byte[], int, int) method in the encoder instance.

---

Please advise which methods would be best locations to fix.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
